findings.note: Clean is a white box with a black border and readable 'SUPER MARIO' label. Charcoal floods the ENTIRE enclosed box body with dense texture, collapsing it into a near-solid dark mass; the white interior and the label text are completely lost. On most other objects charcoal correctly preserves white interiors, so the fully-enclosed dark-bordered rectangle is being mis-classified as a fillable region instead of paper-white.
findings.researchedFix: Drive charcoal/stipple texture DENSITY from per-region source luminance with a highlight threshold: pixels/regions above a luminance threshold are left as paper (no marks), and only sub-threshold regions accumulate marks (dots closer together = darker, fewer dots = lighter, paper showing through for highlights). Do not fill an enclosed white region just because it has a dark border — classify it by its own fill luminance, not by its outline.

findings.note: Same as charcoal: Clean's white box + 'SUPER MARIO' label becomes a dense, featureless dark stipple mass. The white field and text knockout are destroyed. Risograph and newsprint on this same object keep the label readable, proving the box is meant to stay light — charcoal/stipple over-fill it.
findings.researchedFix: Map stipple dot density to source darkness with a white/highlight cutoff so light regions stay as bare paper (the canonical stipple rule: dot spacing proportional to local darkness, paper left visible for highlights). Apply the texture only to regions whose own luminance is below threshold, never to an enclosed white panel.

findings.note: Clean shows a white amp body with a dark top bar and a white interior panel containing thin horizontal divider lines. Risograph floods the whole silhouette with a flat mid/dark gray: the white interior panel is shaded gray and the divider lines are nearly swallowed. Charcoal, stipple, newsprint, outline-only and wireframe all keep the interior white in this same row, so risograph is the outlier.
findings.researchedFix: Render risograph as a flat SPOT-COLOR ink layer over a white substrate with halftone dots and alpha-blend compositing, not as a solid silhouette flood. Tone should be carried by halftone dot size so paper-white knockout regions stay white; separate the artwork into ink layers (dark bar = ink, interior panel = paper) instead of filling the whole shape.

findings.note: Clean is a white card with a dotted border and a dark asterisk on a white field. Risograph fills the card body mid-gray, shading the white field (asterisk survives but the paper-white is gone). Other styles keep the card white.
findings.researchedFix: Use risograph spot-ink-over-paper compositing with halftone screening so the card body remains paper-white; only the asterisk and border become ink. Tonal areas should be expressed via halftone dot coverage, preserving substrate white in knockout regions.

findings.note: Clean is a light shirt with readable 'PUNK' text. Risograph floods the shirt dark gray and the PUNK text loses contrast/legibility. Charcoal, stipple, newsprint, outline-only, wireframe keep the shirt light and PUNK readable.
findings.researchedFix: Composite risograph as translucent ink over a white substrate with halftone dots; keep the shirt body in a light ink/paper tone and render PUNK as a knockout (paper showing through) or separate ink layer so it stays legible rather than flooding the silhouette solid.

findings.note: Clean is a boarding pass with a white main body, a light-gray stub on the right separated by a perforation line, and 'BOG -> JFK' text. Risograph floods the entire pass dark gray: the white-body-vs-gray-stub distinction collapses and the text is barely legible. Charcoal and stipple preserve the body, perforation, and text.
findings.researchedFix: Separate tones into spot-ink layers over white paper and apply halftone screening so the white body stays paper-white, the stub becomes a lighter halftone tint (not a solid flood), and the perforation/text remain as crisp ink. Preserve substrate white in the body region rather than filling the whole silhouette.

findings.note: Clean is a light foil pack with horizontal seam lines and a dark 'P-SMN' label box. Risograph floods the whole pack dark gray, shading the white body and seams and reducing the label to barely visible. Charcoal and stipple keep the pack body light with a readable label.
findings.researchedFix: Render risograph via halftone spot-ink over white substrate so the pack body stays light (paper or a light halftone tint), seams stay as ink lines, and the label box remains a distinct ink region — instead of a uniform silhouette fill that erases the white body.

findings.note: Clean is a white binder holding a 3x4 grid of white card pockets (knockouts) with gray grid lines. Risograph floods the binder mid-gray and the nine white pockets become shaded gray, losing their knockout separation. bold-ink, outline-only and wireframe keep the pockets white.
findings.researchedFix: Fill regions respecting holes/knockouts using the even-odd fill rule so the pocket interiors are left unfilled (paper), and render risograph as halftone spot-ink over white rather than a solid silhouette flood. Provide the pocket shapes as inner sub-polygons so even-odd leaves them as substrate white.

findings.note: Clean is a white binder page with a dark left spine binding and readable 'PKMN COLLECTION' text. Risograph floods the body mid-gray so the white page is shaded and the dark spine no longer reads as darker than the body (tonal separation collapses). Charcoal and stipple keep the white body, dark spine, and text distinct.
findings.researchedFix: Separate the artwork into spot-ink layers over white paper (spine = solid ink, page body = paper/light halftone tint, text = knockout) and use halftone screening for tone. This keeps the dark-spine-vs-light-body contrast and legible text instead of averaging the whole shape to one gray.

findings.note: Clean is a white card sleeve with a thin outline and a small dark mark centered. Risograph fills the sleeve body mid/dark gray, shading the white card field. Other styles keep the sleeve white with just the outline and mark.
findings.researchedFix: Render risograph as halftone spot-ink over white so the sleeve body stays paper-white and only the outline and center mark become ink; carry any tone via halftone dots rather than a flat body flood.

findings.note: Clean shows a light bottle opener body with a white knockout hole at the handle end. Risograph floods the body dark gray, shading the white body (the hole survives as a faint lighter disc but the body white is lost). Stipple and newsprint keep the body light with the hole clearly open.
findings.researchedFix: Use halftone spot-ink over white substrate for risograph and apply the even-odd fill rule for the handle hole so it stays unfilled; keep the body as a light ink/paper tone rather than a solid flood so the knockout reads clearly.

findings.note: Clean (sheet-024 row 8) is a folded-flag triangle with a 4-tier tonal gradient: black apex, dark-grey, mid-grey, then a LIGHT-grey base band. The charcoal variant collapses the whole triangle into a near-solid black scribbled mass; the light base tier reads dark (white-shaded) and all intermediate tonal steps merge, so the defining stepped tonal/stripe structure of the folded flag is lost. Confirmed via 4x zoom (/tmp/aud/r08-clean.png vs /tmp/aud/r08-charcoal.png). The stipple variant in the same row preserved the gradient via dot density, proving the source tone data exists and only the charcoal path discards it.
findings.researchedFix: Replace the binarize-to-solid-ink fill with ordered-dithering / threshold-map quantization (Bayer threshold map, designed specifically to minimize the perceptual difference between a grayscale image and its quantization), or cel-shading-style tonal quantization that maps each region's source luminance to a discrete shade band. Sample source luminance per fill region and modulate charcoal stroke density/spacing to that luminance instead of flooding every fill at one ink value, so the relative lightness ordering (apex dark -> base light) survives.

findings.note: Same row 8 (sheet-024). Risograph flattens the 4-tier tonal gradient into a single dark grey-to-black mass; the light base band is darkened (white-shaded) and the mid-tone steps blob together, erasing the folded-flag stripe identity. Confirmed via 4x zoom (/tmp/aud/r08-risograph.png) against /tmp/aud/r08-clean.png. Risograph's 2-tone posterization is correct behaviour for other rows where it preserved interior detail, but here it posterizes a graded form to one tone and loses the object's defining structure.
findings.researchedFix: Use posterization with MORE than one ink level (quantize to the same number of discrete tone bands present in the source, i.e. cel-shading quantization to N shades) rather than a single dark fill, and/or apply a halftone screen whose dot size tracks source luminance per region (digital halftoning) so the graded bands map to distinct dot densities and remain separable.

findings.note: Clean (sheet-036 row 2) is THREE separate domino tiles stacked vertically, each split with pip dots. The rough-handdrawn variant collapses the three tiles into a single illegible dark scribbled blob - the three-instance stack and the pips are destroyed. Confirmed via 4x zoom (/tmp/aud/r2dom-clean.png vs /tmp/aud/r2dom-rough.png). The right-half styles (risograph, newsprint, outline-only, wireframe) rendered all three tiles correctly, so the source group has three children and only the hand-drawn render path drops/merges them.
findings.researchedFix: Traverse the SVG DOM and sketch EACH element/subpath separately instead of treating the merged group as one path (the svg2roughjs approach: preprocess + flatten the SVG tree and render every child element with Rough.js individually; Rough.js returns one <g> node per shape). Iterate the group's children / each moveto-delimited subpath and emit an independent hand-drawn stroke set per instance so all three tiles and their pips survive.

findings.note: Sheet-036 row 2. Sketchy renders only ONE domino tile; the other two of the three-tile stack are dropped. Confirmed via 4x zoom (/tmp/aud/r2dom-sketchy.png) vs Clean's three tiles. Same group-collapse failure as rough-handdrawn but resolves to a single legible tile rather than a blob.
findings.researchedFix: Same fix: iterate over the group's child elements / subpaths and render each domino instance separately via Rough.js (svg2roughjs traverses and sketches each element), rather than rendering only the first/merged shape.

findings.note: Sheet-036 row 2. Bold-ink renders only ONE domino tile instead of the three in Clean. Confirmed via 4x zoom (/tmp/aud/r2dom-boldink.png). Two of three group instances dropped.
findings.researchedFix: Render each group child / subpath as its own stroked path so all three tiles draw (svg2roughjs-style per-element traversal); do not collapse the multi-instance group to a single render call.

findings.note: Sheet-036 row 2. Wet-ink renders only ONE domino tile; the three-tile vertical stack is reduced to one. Confirmed via 4x zoom (/tmp/aud/r2dom-wetink.png).
findings.researchedFix: Iterate the group's children / subpaths and apply the wet-ink stroke treatment per instance instead of once on a merged shape (svg2roughjs per-element rendering).

findings.note: Sheet-036 row 2. Charcoal renders only ONE domino tile rather than the three in Clean. Confirmed via 4x zoom (/tmp/aud/r2dom-charcoal.png). Consistent with the whole hand-drawn family collapsing this 3-instance group, while risograph/newsprint/outline/wireframe kept all three.
findings.researchedFix: Apply per-element/per-subpath rendering so each of the three tiles is drawn independently (svg2roughjs traverses and sketches each child element), instead of rendering a single merged fill region.

findings.note: Clean US flag has a SOLID-BLACK canton plus solid-black stripe bands. Sketchy renders the canton and dark stripes as outline-only scribbles on white — the solid-dark fill regions are dropped, so the flag loses all its filled mass and reads as an empty grid. Same failure in rough-handdrawn (canton hollow) and partially bold-ink (canton an empty ruled box, not filled).
findings.researchedFix: Use Tonal Art Maps / Real-Time Hatching (Praun, Hoppe, Webb, Finkelstein 2001): map the source region's darkness to hatch-stroke DENSITY so a solid-black region becomes dense hatching (darker tones generated by adding strokes onto lighter tones), never bare outline. The sketchy/rough generators must fill filled regions with tonal hatching clipped to the region boundary instead of discarding interior fill.

findings.note: Clean has a SOLID-BLACK picture window (whole interior filled black) with a small light figure knocked out. Sketchy renders the interior as plain white with only scribbled frame outlines — the entire black fill is dropped. Rough-handdrawn drops it identically; bold-ink also shows a white interior (large black fill lost, only a header bar drawn).
findings.researchedFix: Tonal Art Maps / Real-Time Hatching (Praun et al.): treat the dark interior as a high-tone region and fill it with progressively-nested hatching strokes whose density tracks the source luminance, clipped to the window boundary, preserving the knocked-out light figure as the un-hatched area. Solid fills should map to maximum hatch density, not be discarded.

findings.note: Clean has a THICK solid-black outer frame band and a small solid-black thumbnail block inside. Sketchy renders the thick frame as a thin scribbled outline and the thumbnail as an empty outlined box — both solid-dark fills are lost. Bold-ink also leaves the thumbnail an empty box (its solid fill dropped).
findings.researchedFix: Tonal Art Maps / Real-Time Hatching (Praun et al.): represent the frame band and thumbnail as tone-filled regions via density-graded hatching mapped to source darkness, clipped to each region, so heavy solid fills survive the sketchy transform as dense strokes rather than collapsing to outline.

findings.note: Clean has a SOLID-DARK portrait frame border around a light photo area. Sketchy reduces the dark border to a thin double-line outline, dropping the filled frame band. Bold-ink likewise draws a hollow ruled rectangle rather than the filled dark border.
findings.researchedFix: Tonal Art Maps / Real-Time Hatching (Praun et al.): map the dark frame band's tone to hatch density (add strokes for darker tone) and clip the strokes to the border region, keeping the light photo area un-hatched — preserving the dark/light contrast instead of flattening the border to outline.

findings.note: Clean tray has a WHITE interior panel with small icons. Risograph floods the entire silhouette with a flat mid-gray ink, shading the white interior panel gray and lowering interior icon contrast — it ignores the white knockout/fill and tints the whole shape.
findings.researchedFix: Knockout-aware duotone with halftone screening: per CSS-Tricks SVG duotone, drive feComponentTransfer with an alpha table (e.g. feFuncA tableValues '0 1') so highlight/white regions map to the LIGHT ink (substrate) instead of the dark ink, and render mid-tones as halftone dots whose coverage encodes tone — never a flat solid flood. Respect the source white fill as unprinted paper.

findings.note: Clean is a white disc with a legible '35mm' label. Risograph fills the disc with a medium-dark gray, dropping the '35mm' text to low-contrast dark-on-dark and nearly swallowing it. The white interior is flooded rather than knocked out.
findings.researchedFix: Knockout-aware duotone + halftone (SVG feComponentTransfer alpha table to keep highlights light; halftone dot-density for tone). Keep the disc face as light substrate so the dark label text stays legible; only the rim/shadow gets ink. Use halftone screening for tone, not a flat gray fill.

findings.note: Clean is a white disc with a ring of WHITE dot-holes and a center hub. Risograph floods the disc dark gray, swallowing the white holes (knockouts) so the perforation pattern disappears into the mass.
findings.researchedFix: Knockout-aware duotone: preserve the source white holes as un-inked substrate (alpha-mapped highlights via feFuncA), and represent the disc tone with halftone dots rather than a solid flood so the white perforations remain visible. Halftone screening converts tone to dot coverage while leaving true whites unprinted.

findings.note: Clean is a white film strip with white sprocket holes and frame divisions. Risograph fills the body dark gray, dropping the white sprocket holes' contrast and compressing the frame divisions into the dark mass.
findings.researchedFix: Knockout-aware duotone + halftone: keep sprocket holes and frame gaps as un-inked substrate via alpha-preserving feComponentTransfer; encode the strip body as halftone dots so internal divisions stay readable rather than flooding flat gray.

findings.note: Clean is a light cylinder with faint surface texture. Risograph fills it near-solid dark gray, losing the surface texture into the mass and shading the light body.
findings.researchedFix: Knockout-aware duotone with halftone screening: map the cylinder's light body to the light ink and render its shading as graduated halftone dots so surface texture survives; do not flood the silhouette with flat dark gray.

findings.note: Clean is a thin frame with a LIGHT/white page interior and a dotted inner border. Risograph floods the interior with a solid dark-gray block, turning the white page into a dark mass and nearly hiding the dotted border.
findings.researchedFix: Knockout-aware duotone: use feComponentTransfer alpha table so the white page maps to light ink (substrate) and stays light; reserve dark ink for actual dark source pixels (the border dots), and use halftone for any mid-tone rather than a flat fill of the whole interior.

findings.note: Clean is a white/clear bottle with a small label band. Risograph fills the bottle near-solid dark gray, shading the clear glass body and reducing the label band to a faint patch — the white body knockout is ignored.
findings.researchedFix: Knockout-aware duotone + halftone: keep the clear glass body as light substrate (alpha-preserving highlight mapping) and represent volume/shading as halftone dot gradients; only the label and edges take ink. Avoid a flat dark flood of the whole silhouette.

findings.note: Clean is a white glass with small WHITE bubble circles inside. Risograph fills the glass dark gray, making the white bubble knockouts invisible against the dark fill.
findings.researchedFix: Knockout-aware duotone: preserve the white bubbles as un-inked substrate via alpha-mapped highlights (feFuncA), and use halftone screening for the glass tone so the bubbles remain visible as light dots rather than being flooded over.

findings.note: Sheet-072 row0. Clean shows a watch body with a white inner screen panel carrying faint text. The risograph variant fills the whole body as one flat mid-grey mass; the inner screen knockout and its text are gone. White inner panel is shaded over and reads as featureless.
findings.researchedFix: Emulate risograph as separate spot-color layers with KNOCKOUT: cut overlapping/interior shapes out of the lower layer so inner panels print as paper-white, then screen each layer with a halftone (Grain Touch dither or Screen-Covered dots) instead of a flat fill. Drive tone with screen frequency/dot size, never a solid fill, so interior knockouts survive.

findings.note: Sheet-072 row1. Clean shows two round knobs over a dark footswitch band. Risograph flattens the body to a solid grey block; the two knobs and the dark band merge into the mass and stop reading as separate features.
findings.researchedFix: Apply the riso fill per sub-shape with knockout separation (knobs and band as their own spot layers cut from the body), then halftone-screen each so knobs stay legible against the body tone rather than dissolving into one flat plate.

findings.note: Sheet-072 row4. Clean shows a camera/projector body with two reels on top and a side lens. Risograph turns the body into a solid dark block and the two reels collapse into it; the light body fill and reel circles are lost.
findings.researchedFix: Risograph layer must preserve the reel circles as interior knockouts (paper-white holes via even-odd) on the body layer, then screen the body tone with a halftone so the reels read as cut-outs rather than being painted over.

findings.note: Sheet-072 row5. Clean is a WHITE card with a center shield/badge and small caption text. Risograph fills the card panel solid grey, shading the white paper and muddying the inner shield and caption.
findings.researchedFix: Set the card paper as the unprinted base (no ink layer) and only screen the badge/text as a separate spot layer; in riso the substrate stays paper-white unless an ink layer explicitly covers it. Use knockout so the shield/text print over an unscreened card, not over a flat grey plate.

findings.note: Sheet-072 row6. Clean shows a body with a large concentric-ring lens and a viewfinder/flash on top. Risograph flattens to a solid dark mass; the concentric lens rings and top details vanish.
findings.researchedFix: Render the concentric lens as nested knockout rings (even-odd compound path) on the riso body layer and screen the body with halftone dots; the ring contrast must come from layered screens, not a single flat fill that buries the rings.

findings.note: Sheet-072 row7. Clean shows a controller body with a joystick circle and button dots. Risograph fills the body solid dark and the stick and dots are absorbed into the mass.
findings.researchedFix: Keep the stick/buttons as interior knockouts on the body spot layer and halftone-screen the body tone so the small features stay as legible cut-outs instead of being over-inked by a flat fill.

findings.note: Sheet-072 row12. Clean shows a can with a readable LACROIX wordmark up top, a light upper body, and a speckled lower flavor band. Risograph fills the can one solid grey; the wordmark and the upper/lower division disappear.
findings.researchedFix: Separate the wordmark and the speckle band as their own spot/halftone layers and knockout the wordmark from the body tone so text prints paper-white; screen the lower band as halftone so the flavor texture survives instead of being flattened.

findings.note: Sheet-084 row0. Clean is a pyramid of ~10 distinct cans. rough-handdrawn collapses the entire stack into a single tiny dark vertical blob; the individual cans are gone. Only outline-only/wireframe (and partly newsprint) preserve the pyramid, which points to a fill/compound-path bug where the disjoint can group is treated as one filled region.
findings.researchedFix: Apply the sketchy fill PER sub-shape, not to the merged group bounds: run the rough.js scan-line hachure on each can outline separately, or set the compound path so disjoint cans are filled by even-odd parity (parity resets per scanline span) rather than collapsing to one bbox. The scan-line polygon fill with odd/even parity handles multiple disjoint regions and holes correctly.

findings.note: Sheet-084 row0. The 10-can pyramid collapses to a tiny stack of 2-3 dark rectangles; most cans are lost. Same disjoint-group fill collapse as the rough-handdrawn variant.
findings.researchedFix: Iterate the sketchy renderer over each can path individually so each gets its own outline+hachure, instead of feeding the union/bbox of all cans. Use even-odd fill-rule on the compound path so separate cans render as separate regions.

findings.note: Sheet-084 row0. The can pyramid renders as a single small dark block; individual cans are not distinguishable.
findings.researchedFix: Stroke/fill each can sub-path independently; ensure the geometry passed in is the multi-subpath set, not a flattened bbox. Compound path should use even-odd so interior gaps between cans stay open.

findings.note: Sheet-084 row0. Pyramid collapses to a solid dark blob with ink bleed; no separate cans survive.
findings.researchedFix: Process per sub-shape and apply the ink-bleed pass per can outline; do not merge the disjoint cans into one filled silhouette. Even-odd parity scan-line fill preserves the gaps between cans.

findings.note: Sheet-084 row0. Pyramid collapses into one small dark textured block; the ~10 cans are lost.
findings.researchedFix: Run the charcoal texture fill on each can region separately via the scan-line fill that supports disjoint regions/holes, rather than texturing one merged silhouette.

findings.note: Sheet-084 row0. The pyramid reduces to a small dark stippled block; individual cans cannot be read.
findings.researchedFix: Generate stipple points per can region (one fill pass per sub-path) so each can gets its own dot field; even-odd parity keeps the inter-can gaps unstippled.

findings.note: Sheet-084 row0. Pyramid collapses to a small dark grey block; cans merged and lost. Combines the disjoint-group fill bug with the riso flat-fill bug.
findings.researchedFix: Treat each can as its own spot/halftone region (per sub-path) with knockout between cans, then screen each; do not merge the stack into one flat plate. Per-region scan-line fill plus even-odd compound handling preserves the cans.

findings.note: Sheet-084 row2. Clean is a white card framing a 3x3 grid of dark poster cells with white gutters. Risograph fills the whole panel solid grey: the white frame and gutters are shaded over and the 3x3 grid is lost into the mass.
findings.researchedFix: Keep the card/gutters as unprinted paper (knockout the white gutters and frame from the ink layer) and screen the 9 poster cells as separate halftone fills; in riso the white must be substrate, not a covered region.

findings.note: Sheet-084 row3. Clean shows a cartridge with a ZELDA label and bottom contact ridges. Risograph fills it solid dark; the label text and ridge lines disappear.
findings.researchedFix: Knockout the label text and ridge lines from the body spot layer (paper-white) and halftone-screen the body tone so the label and contacts stay legible over an unscreened cut-out instead of a flat fill.

findings.note: Sheet-084 row4. Clean is a WHITE sheet with text lines and a dark heart. Risograph fills the sheet solid grey, shading the white paper and burying most of the text lines; the heart barely reads.
findings.researchedFix: Leave the paper unprinted (no ink layer over the sheet) and screen only the text lines and heart as a spot layer; substrate stays paper-white in riso unless explicitly inked.

findings.note: Sheet-084 row5. Clean shows a mask with white eye-hole knockouts and a mouth. Risograph fills the face one solid dark oval; the eye holes are shaded over and the mouth/contours are lost.
findings.researchedFix: Render eye/mouth holes as even-odd interior knockouts on the face spot layer so they stay paper-white, then halftone-screen the face tone; the holes must be cut-outs, not over-inked.

findings.note: Sheet-084 row6. Clean is a light tag with horizontal text lines and a loop. Risograph fills it solid grey; the text lines are absorbed into the fill.
findings.researchedFix: Knockout the text lines from the tag spot layer and screen the tag tone with halftone so the lines read as paper-white cut-outs rather than vanishing under a flat fill.

findings.note: Sheet-084 row7. Clean shows a worn tag with a '303' number. Risograph fills it solid grey and the 303 is lost into the mass.
findings.researchedFix: Knockout the numerals from the tag spot layer (paper-white) and halftone-screen the body so the number stays legible instead of being over-inked.

findings.note: Sheet-084 row8. Clean is a light closed-laptop top with a small center logo dot. Risograph fills the body solid dark and the logo dot is lost.
findings.researchedFix: Keep the logo as an interior knockout (even-odd hole) on the body layer and screen the body tone; the small mark must survive as a paper-white cut-out, not be painted over.

findings.note: Sheet-084 row11. Clean shows a cap dome with a circular 'M' emblem. Risograph fills the dome solid grey; the emblem circle and its white knockout are lost.
findings.researchedFix: Render the emblem as a separate spot layer with knockout (the M and emblem ring cut from the dome tone), then halftone-screen the dome so the emblem reads as a layered mark rather than dissolving into a flat fill.

findings.note: Sheet-084 row12. Clean shows a keyboard with rows of individual keys. Risograph flattens it to a solid dark grey mass; the entire key grid is lost. Other fill styles keep the keys discernible, so this is specific to the riso flat fill.
findings.researchedFix: Knockout the inter-key gutters from the body spot layer (paper-white grid lines via even-odd compound) and halftone-screen the keytops so the grid survives; alternatively overlay the key edge line-work on top of the screened tone, since halftone with preserved edge line-work keeps the grid legible.

findings.note: Clean medallion = concentric rings with a WHITE inner center disc + small detail; ribbon is light/outlined. Risograph fills the entire silhouette with flat opaque mid-grey ink: the rings, the white center disc, and the ribbon collapse into one featureless mass. Every other style (sketchy/bold/charcoal/stipple/outline/wireframe) keeps the ring structure and white center. Riso ignores the interior knockout.
findings.researchedFix: Don't paint the riso flat fill opaque over the whole silhouette: (a) build the fill as a compound path that respects holes via fill-rule='evenodd' so the white inner disc stays unfilled, and (b) render interior detail strokes ON TOP of the fill using SVG paint-order (paint the stroke after the fill). Practically, riso workflow says use a Multiply ink + Tone-Lift on midtones so detail doesn't 'collapse into one heavy ink mass'.

findings.note: Clean cone has parallel ridge lines with WHITE gaps between them and a separate handle. Risograph fills the cone and handle as one flat dark mass; the inter-rib white gaps are shaded over and the ridge lines vanish. charcoal/stipple/outline/wireframe all keep the ribs.
findings.researchedFix: Apply the riso ink as a translucent Multiply layer (not opaque) and keep the ridge-line strokes as a separate detail layer painted above the fill (NPR layered stroke ordering / SVG paint-order='stroke'); the white inter-rib gaps must remain paper-reserve, which riso guides achieve by keeping detail as knockout rather than overprinting solid.

findings.note: Clean mic head is a rounded grille with horizontal WHITE gap lines. Risograph renders the head as a flat dark-grey solid dome; the grille lines are filled over and lost. bold-ink keeps the grille as darker bands; all lighter styles keep it clearly.
findings.researchedFix: Preserve the grille as a detail-stroke layer drawn over the riso fill (SVG paint-order), and use a Multiply ink so the head reads as tone rather than an opaque mass; riso tonal guidance: keep midtones lifted so the grille doesn't collapse into solid ink.

findings.note: Clean = square body (light) with an inner WHITE square panel + central hub circle + center dot. Risograph fills the whole square flat dark grey; inner panel, hub circle and dot all crush into a near-featureless mass. bold-ink/charcoal/outline/wireframe keep panel+circle.
findings.researchedFix: Use evenodd compound-path fill so the inner white panel is a true hole (unfilled), and paint hub/dot detail strokes above the fill via paint-order; treat riso ink as Multiply not opaque so structure survives.

findings.note: Clean = woven bag with horizontal patterned bands (zigzag/diamond motifs over WHITE ground). Risograph fills the bag flat dark grey; the woven pattern bands and white grounds are entirely lost into one solid mass. Every other style preserves the weave pattern.
findings.researchedFix: Keep the pattern motifs as a knockout detail layer over a translucent Multiply base fill (riso multiply-layer practice), so the white ground between motifs stays paper-reserve; alternatively render the pattern strokes above the fill with SVG paint-order.

findings.note: Clean octagonal moka pot has a chamber-division waist line separating top/bottom chambers. Risograph fills the body flat dark grey and the chamber-division line is lost into the mass. All other styles keep the waist line.
findings.researchedFix: Render the chamber-division line as a detail stroke painted on top of the fill (SVG paint-order), and use Multiply ink so the body reads as flat color with the seam still legible rather than an opaque blob.

findings.note: Clean = vertical tube with a WHITE body and a central label band of small dots/buttons. Risograph fills the tube a dark solid bar; the white body is shaded over and the label-band detail survives only as faint marks. charcoal/stipple/outline/wireframe keep the label band on a light body.
findings.researchedFix: Keep the tube body as paper-reserve under a Multiply ink (don't fill opaque), and place the label-band detail as a stroke/knockout layer above the fill via SVG paint-order; riso guidance: avoid heavy solid fills over detail.

findings.note: Clean monitor: bezel (mid tone) with a distinctly lighter SCREEN panel inside + stand. Risograph fills bezel, screen and base all the same flat dark grey; the bezel-vs-screen distinction is destroyed (screen knockout shaded to bezel tone). Every other style keeps the screen panel lighter than the bezel.
findings.researchedFix: Treat the screen as a separate lighter region (compound path with evenodd, or its own tone) so it isn't filled to the same value as the bezel; use Multiply layering / tone-lift to retain the two distinct tonal planes instead of one opaque mass.

findings.note: Clean = light-grey mouse top with a visible scroll-wheel / button-split line. Risograph fills the mouse a flat dark-grey solid oval; the wheel/button-split detail is lost into the fill (only a faint mark). charcoal/stipple/newsprint keep a light body with the wheel readable.
findings.researchedFix: Paint the scroll-wheel/button-split as a detail stroke layer above the riso fill (SVG paint-order) and keep the body as Multiply tone not opaque ink so the split line stays legible.

findings.note: Clean = 3-prong controller (white body) with central button cluster (A/B, d-pad, analog). Risograph fuses all 3 prongs into a flat dark-grey mass; prong divisions and most button detail are lost (only the center stick barely survives). outline/wireframe/charcoal keep prong seams + buttons.
findings.researchedFix: Render the prong-seam and button strokes above the riso fill via SVG paint-order, and use evenodd holes for any knockout button rings; keep ink Multiply so the body is tone, not an opaque blob (riso: don't let detail collapse into one ink mass).

findings.note: Clean bottle has a WHITE body with label markings (squares/lines) and a darker cap. Risograph fills the whole body flat dark grey; label markings are lost into the fill and the white body is shaded over. Every other style keeps the label marks on a light body.
findings.researchedFix: Keep bottle body as paper-reserve / Multiply tone and render label markings as a knockout/stroke detail layer above the fill (SVG paint-order); riso practice avoids heavy solid fills over fine label detail.

findings.note: Clean = cartridge with a WHITE label panel (text) and ridge lines below. Risograph fills the cartridge flat dark grey; the white label panel is shaded (text barely survives) and the ridge lines are lost. bold/charcoal/outline/wireframe keep the white label + ridges.
findings.researchedFix: Make the label panel a true hole via fill-rule='evenodd' compound path so it stays white, and paint ridge-line + text strokes over the fill with SVG paint-order; use Multiply ink for the body tone.

findings.note: Clean = rectangular controller, WHITE face, with d-pad (+), select/start (--) and A/B buttons. Risograph fills the body flat dark grey crushing the white face contrast; controls survive only faintly. Every other style keeps the light face with crisp controls.
findings.researchedFix: Keep the face as paper-reserve under Multiply ink and render the d-pad/buttons as a detail-stroke layer above the fill (SVG paint-order); tone-lift midtones so controls stay legible per riso guidance.

findings.note: Clean = round cat face (WHITE face) with ears, two eyes and a smile. Risograph fills the face a flat dark-grey solid circle; the white face is shaded and the smile/eyes are crushed into the mass (eyes only faintly darker). Every other style keeps a light face with clear eyes + smile. Classic 'face vanishes into form' failure.
findings.researchedFix: Render face features (eyes, smile) as a detail-stroke layer painted on TOP of the riso fill (SVG paint-order), and use a Multiply ink with lifted midtones so the face reads as tone, not solid — riso tonal guidance explicitly says higher midtone values 'preserve facial detail instead of letting shadows collapse into one heavy ink mass'.

findings.note: Clean = magazine cover: dark masthead band over a WHITE cover field with a central white-bordered circle. Risograph fills the whole cover flat dark grey; the white field and the central light circle are crushed to near-black, masthead lost. Every other style keeps the white field + circle.
findings.researchedFix: Use evenodd compound paths so the cover field and central circle stay as white holes, and place the masthead as its own darker region; render type/circle detail above the fill via paint-order and use Multiply ink rather than one opaque mass.

findings.note: Clean = headband + two earcups drawn as rings with concentric inner detail. Risograph fills the earcups as flat dark-grey solid discs; the concentric ring detail is lost. clean/charcoal/wireframe keep the rings.
findings.researchedFix: Keep the inner cup ring as a knockout (evenodd hole) and/or render concentric detail strokes over the fill via SVG paint-order; use Multiply tone so the cups aren't opaque solid discs.

findings.note: Clean = stacked pouches with WHITE faces and zipper/seam lines. Risograph fills the stack flat dark grey; face divisions and zipper lines are lost and the white faces shaded over. Other styles keep seams + light faces.
findings.researchedFix: Keep pouch faces as paper-reserve / Multiply tone and render zipper/seam strokes above the fill (SVG paint-order); riso practice: avoid heavy solid fills over fine seam detail.

findings.note: Clean = two mugs with WHITE bodies and open handles. Risograph fills both mugs flat dark-grey solid; the white bodies are shaded over (handle openings survive only as outline notches). Every other style keeps light bodies.
findings.researchedFix: Keep mug bodies as paper-reserve under Multiply ink (don't opaque-fill) and ensure the handle opening is a true evenodd hole; this matches riso 'discard white knockout / preserve overprint' practice so whites stay unprinted.

findings.note: Clean = vertical photo strip with 4 WHITE photo-frame windows. Risograph fills the strip a dark-grey solid bar; the 4 white windows are crushed (only faint internal lines). outline/wireframe keep all 4 frames open.
findings.researchedFix: Model the 4 frame windows as evenodd holes so they remain white, and paint frame borders above the fill via SVG paint-order; use Multiply tone for the strip body rather than an opaque bar.

findings.note: Clean = passport booklet (light cover) with a WHITE emblem circle + 'PASSPORT' text. Risograph fills the booklet flat dark grey; the emblem and text are crushed and the light cover is shaded over. Every other style keeps the emblem + text on a light cover.
findings.researchedFix: Keep the cover as paper-reserve / Multiply tone, model the emblem ring as an evenodd knockout, and render emblem + type as a detail layer above the fill (SVG paint-order).

findings.note: Clean cover is ALREADY dark with light/white knockout text rows + a white emblem ring, plus a lighter back page. Newsprint converts the dark cover into a uniform dense black halftone-dot field: the knockout text and emblem ring are lost under the dots and the back page nearly disappears. (Risograph on this row was acceptable — it lightened the cover to grey and kept layout — so this is a newsprint-specific failure, not riso.)
findings.researchedFix: Cap the halftone dot density / use a threshold so knockout whites survive: in halftone workflows enable 'Ignore White' and a ~50% threshold so light (text/emblem) pixels become paper-white and only true darks become dots; render the knockout text/emblem as a white detail layer above the halftone so it isn't filled in.

findings.note: Clean is a SOLID BLACK slide cover with white knockout 'DD' logo + text/underline. rough-handdrawn renders an EMPTY white box with only a sketchy outline: the entire dark fill AND the white knockout content vanish. Verified at 2x zoom (/tmp/pitch_clean.png vs /tmp/pitch_rough.png). Same emptying occurs in sketchy and bold-ink for this object.
findings.researchedFix: rough.js (the hand-drawn/sketchy engine) renders NO fill unless an explicit fill color is passed alongside fillStyle ('Without specifying a fill color, no fill renders regardless of fillStyle choice'). Carry the source SVG's fill attribute (#000) into rough.js options as fill:'#000', fillStyle:'solid' (use 'hachure'/'cross-hatch' only for tonal grays). The SVG->rough conversion is currently passing stroke but dropping fill, so solid-black regions collapse to outline.

findings.note: Clean SOLID BLACK cover with white knockout text becomes a clean EMPTY outlined rectangle in bold-ink, no fill and no text. Verified at 2x (/tmp/pitch_bold.png).
findings.researchedFix: Same root cause: bold-ink path passes stroke but not fill to rough.js. Set fill:'#000' + fillStyle:'solid' for shapes whose source fill is dark; render white knockout text as overprinted paper-colored glyphs on top of the solid fill.

findings.note: Same as rough/bold: the black cover + knockout text render as an empty sketchy box, dark fill dropped.
findings.researchedFix: Propagate source fill color into rough.js fill option with fillStyle:'solid'; sketchy roughness applies to the fill hatching/edges, not to whether the fill exists.

findings.note: Clean is a thick BLACK frame, PURE-WHITE interior panel, PURE-BLACK bottle silhouette, black PERRIER text on white. Risograph floods the white interior panel to light gray and drops the black bottle to mid-gray, so figure and ground collapse to nearly one tone. Verified at 2x (/tmp/perrier_clean.png vs /tmp/perrier_risograph.png). Note: pinnedFigurePhoto/risograph does NOT fail because its Clean interior was already gray.
findings.researchedFix: Authentic risograph is a duotone/spot-color separation that PRESERVES luminosity: map darkest tones -> ink, lightest tones -> paper-white, only colors change. Replace the uniform mid-gray flood with a gradient-map/threshold (white point stays paper, black figure stays ink) so the white knockout panel renders as paper and the bottle stays a distinct dark spot color, keeping figure-ground contrast.

findings.note: Clean has a SOLID BLACK display panel on the glove body. bold-ink renders that panel as an EMPTY white box with a small button-grid outline; the solid dark fill is gone. Verified at 2x (/tmp/pglove_clean.png vs /tmp/pglove_bold.png). Sketchy/rough show the same light-grid treatment of the dark panel.
findings.researchedFix: Carry the panel's source fill (#000) into rough.js as fill + fillStyle:'solid'. The conversion currently sends only the panel's stroke outline, so the knockout dark panel renders empty.

findings.note: Clean is a SOLID BLACK poster with white knockout text 'WRESTLE MANIA / XL'. rough-handdrawn renders an EMPTY outlined rectangle: dark fill and text both gone. (sketchy and bold-ink identical.) tone styles wet-ink/charcoal/stipple/risograph correctly keep dark+text.
findings.researchedFix: Same rough.js fill-dropping bug. Pass fill:'#000', fillStyle:'solid'; render knockout text by overprinting paper-colored glyphs over the filled rect.

findings.note: Solid black poster + knockout text render as an empty sketchy outline box.
findings.researchedFix: Propagate fill color into rough.js fill with fillStyle:'solid'; sketchy roughness should affect fill edges only, not fill presence.

findings.note: Solid black poster + knockout text render as a clean empty outlined rectangle.
findings.researchedFix: Set fill:'#000' + fillStyle:'solid' from the source SVG fill; overprint knockout text on top.

findings.note: Clean is a CD case with a LARGE BLACK label holding white knockout 'FINAL FANTASY' text. bold-ink renders the whole label area WHITE/EMPTY (only header strip + bottom teeth survive as outlines); dark fill and all knockout text gone. Verified at 2x (/tmp/jewel_clean.png vs /tmp/jewel_bold.png). rough-handdrawn and sketchy empty it the same way.
findings.researchedFix: Carry the label's source fill into rough.js (fill:'#000', fillStyle:'solid'); the per-shape fill is being dropped during SVG->rough conversion so only stroked sub-shapes (header, teeth) survive.

findings.note: Large black label + knockout text render as an empty sketchy box; only header/teeth outlines remain.
findings.researchedFix: Propagate fill color into rough.js fill option with fillStyle:'solid'.

findings.note: Black label area dropped to white outline; knockout text lost.
findings.researchedFix: Set fill from source SVG (#000) + fillStyle:'solid'; sketchy randomness applies to fill, not its existence.

findings.note: Clean has a SOLID BLACK label strip on the card body. bold-ink renders that strip as an EMPTY white box (outline only). Verified at 2x (/tmp/memcard_clean.png vs /tmp/memcard_bold.png). rough-handdrawn and sketchy drop it likewise.
findings.researchedFix: Pass the strip's source fill into rough.js as fill + fillStyle:'solid'; conversion currently omits fill for this sub-shape.

findings.note: Clean is a SOLID BLACK poster with white knockout 'PS / DREAMS' text. rough-handdrawn renders an EMPTY outlined rectangle; dark fill + text gone. (sketchy and bold-ink identical.) tone styles keep dark+text.
findings.researchedFix: Same rough.js fill-dropping bug; set fill:'#000', fillStyle:'solid' and overprint knockout text.

findings.note: Solid black poster + knockout text render as an empty sketchy outline.
findings.researchedFix: Propagate fill color to rough.js fill with fillStyle:'solid'.

findings.note: Solid black poster + knockout text render as a clean empty outlined box.
findings.researchedFix: Set fill:'#000' + fillStyle:'solid' from source SVG fill; overprint knockout text.

findings.note: Clean has a dark header label strip (grade '10') above the white card window. rough-handdrawn renders that dark header as a light outline (fill dropped); the card window/star detail survives. Milder instance of the same bug (smaller dark region). sketchy shows the same header drop.
findings.researchedFix: Carry the header strip's source fill into rough.js (fill + fillStyle:'solid'); same per-shape fill-propagation fix as the posters/labels.

findings.note: Sheet 144 row7. In Clean the top header is a SOLID DARK rectangle with white knockout 'BOOSTER BOX' text. In bold-ink it renders as an EMPTY OUTLINE rectangle — the dark fill and its knockout text are dropped entirely. Same drop also seen in this row's sketchy and rough-handdrawn tiles; wet-ink/charcoal/risograph correctly keep the band dark. Worst in bold-ink, which should be the heaviest ink yet shows the lightest header. Root cause: the sketch-style transform passes only the path outline to the Rough.js-style renderer and discards the source element's fill paint, so filled regions collapse to outlines.
findings.researchedFix: In Rough.js (the engine these sketch styles use), a shape only gets a filled interior if you explicitly pass fill + fillStyle. Carry the source element's non-transparent fill paint through the style transform and emit it as fill:<originalColor> with fillStyle:'solid' (use 'cross-hatch'/'hachure' with hachureGap/fillWeight for the textured styles) so dark-filled regions stay filled and white knockout text is preserved as negative space — rather than stroking the outline only.

findings.note: Sheet 156 row10. In Clean the top header is a SOLID DARK band with white knockout 'CARTAGENA' text (plus a dark base strip and dark mountain silhouette). In bold-ink the header band renders as an EMPTY OUTLINE rectangle — dark fill and knockout text dropped. Same drop in this row's rough-handdrawn and sketchy tiles; wet-ink and charcoal correctly preserve the dark header with legible knockout text. Identical root cause to sealedBoosterBox: the style transform strokes the outline but discards the element's fill paint, so the solid-dark knockout region becomes a hollow outline.
findings.researchedFix: Same Rough.js fill-preservation technique: thread the original fill color into the sketch renderer and call with fill:<color> + fillStyle:'solid' so filled regions render filled and the knockout text reads as negative space. SVG fill is painted before stroke (W3C SVG painting model), so a region that has a fill in Clean must be given an explicit fill in the transformed output instead of outline-only.

findings.note: Clean has a SOLID BLACK screen filling the bezel. The bold-ink variant renders the screen as an empty white box with only a bold outline rectangle inside - the dark screen region is gone. bold-ink should keep solid fills as solid black; instead it stripped the fill. (Texture-fill siblings wet-ink/charcoal/stipple/newsprint and risograph all correctly represent the dark screen.)
findings.researchedFix: In Rough.js (the canonical hand-drawn/sketch SVG renderer) a filled region is preserved via the `fillStyle` option rather than dropped. For an emphatic-ink look, set `fill` to the source color and `fillStyle:'solid'` so the dark screen renders as a true filled black region; never emit stroke-only when the source path has a non-empty fill. Map source fill darkness -> fillStyle (solid for near-black) so bold-ink keeps solid knockout regions black.

findings.note: Clean's solid black screen renders as an empty white outline-only trapezoid in the sketchy variant - the dark region is dropped to white. A hand-sketch style should still indicate the dark screen with scribble/hatch fill (as wet-ink and charcoal do), not leave it blank.
findings.researchedFix: Use Rough.js hachure/cross-hatch fill to convey tone instead of dropping the fill: keep the source `fill` and set `fillStyle:'hachure'` (or `'cross-hatch'` for darker tone), tuning `hachureGap`/`fillWeight` so darker source fills get denser lines. This is the tonal-art-map / pen-and-ink approach where stroke density encodes tone, preserving the dark screen as dense sketchy hatching.

findings.note: Clean's solid black screen renders as an empty white outline in the rough-handdrawn variant - the dark interior region is lost to white, leaving only a wobbly bezel and inner outline.
findings.researchedFix: Same outline-family root cause: convert the source solid fill to a hand-drawn hatch fill rather than discarding it. Per Rough.js, retain `fill` and apply `fillStyle:'hachure'`/`'cross-hatch'` with `fillWeight`/`hachureGap` mapped from source darkness so the dark screen reads as dense rough hatching, not empty white.

findings.note: Clean has a DARK (black) lower panel under the white VHS label. The bold-ink variant renders that lower panel as an empty white box with only an outline - the solid dark panel is dropped. wet-ink correctly fills the same panel with texture.
findings.researchedFix: bold-ink must preserve solid knockout regions: keep the source `fill` and render with Rough.js `fillStyle:'solid'` so the lower panel stays a filled black region. The renderer should branch on whether the source path has a non-empty fill and never reduce a filled region to stroke-only.

findings.note: Clean's dark lower panel becomes an empty white box (outline only) in the sketchy variant. The dark region is dropped to white instead of being hatch-filled.
findings.researchedFix: Convert the panel's solid fill to sketchy hatching: retain source `fill` and use Rough.js `fillStyle:'hachure'` (or `'cross-hatch'` for the dark tone) with density (hachureGap/fillWeight) driven by source darkness. Tonal-art-map / pen-and-ink theory: encode dark tone as dense line fill, not omission.

findings.note: Clean's dark lower panel renders as an empty white box in the rough-handdrawn variant - solid dark region lost, only wobbly outlines remain.
findings.researchedFix: Same fix as the other outline-family styles: keep the source `fill` and apply a Rough.js hand-drawn fill (`fillStyle:'hachure'`/`'cross-hatch'`) scaled by source darkness instead of discarding the fill, so the dark panel reads as rough hatching.

findings.note: Clean has a SOLID BLACK sleeve background (with a white PUNK/SIDE A label box) and a dark record disc peeking out. The bold-ink variant drops the black sleeve background to white and renders the disc as a hollow circle - both dark regions lost, only bold outlines remain.
findings.researchedFix: Preserve filled regions in bold-ink via Rough.js `fillStyle:'solid'` keeping the source `fill`, so the sleeve background stays solid black and the disc stays a filled dark circle. Do not strip fills on paths whose source fill is non-empty.

findings.note: Clean's solid black sleeve background renders as plain white with only outlines + PUNK text in the sketchy variant - the dominant dark region of the object is gone.
findings.researchedFix: Map the sleeve's solid fill to sketchy hatch fill: retain source `fill`, use Rough.js `fillStyle:'hachure'`/`'cross-hatch'` with line density set from source darkness (hachureGap/fillWeight) so the black sleeve reads as dense hand-drawn hatching, following the tonal-art-map tone-by-density principle.

findings.note: Clean's solid black sleeve background renders as white outlines only in the rough-handdrawn variant; the dark sleeve and dark disc are both dropped.
findings.researchedFix: Same outline-family root cause and fix: keep source `fill` and convert solid dark regions to Rough.js hand-drawn hatch/cross-hatch fill (density from source darkness) rather than emitting stroke-only, so the sleeve and disc retain their dark tone.

findings.note: Clean shows a DARK upper panel with a WHITE knockout figure icon, over a white OLYMPIC label strip. In sketchy the dark upper panel renders WHITE/empty (outline only), so the figure no longer reads as a knockout and the panel's solid value is lost. wet-ink, charcoal, stipple, newsprint all keep the panel dark here, so this is sketchy-specific, not the intended outline mode.
findings.researchedFix: sketchy should fill the closed dark region as a region fill (rough.js fillStyle other than a pure outline) using the source path's compound geometry; the figure stays a knockout via SVG fill-rule='evenodd' on the compound path so the inner icon punches a hole in the filled panel rather than being lost. Apply hachure/cross-hatch fill to the dark region instead of stroking only its border.

findings.note: bold-ink is a heavy-ink style yet the DARK upper panel renders as white/empty with the figure drawn dark-on-white (value inverted). The solid dark panel of Clean is dropped, unlike wet-ink/charcoal which keep it filled.
findings.researchedFix: bold-ink must treat Clean's filled (dark) regions as fills, not as strokes: detect filled subpaths from the source and emit a solid/dense fill for them, preserving the white figure via fill-rule='evenodd' compound-path holes so the knockout is retained instead of inverted.

findings.note: Clean has a DARK header band (white tick marks inside it) above the figure. In sketchy the header band renders WHITE/empty (outline only) and the figure torso also loses its dark fill. wet-ink, charcoal, stipple, newsprint keep the header dark, confirming this is a sketchy fill failure, not outline mode.
findings.researchedFix: Same root fix: region-fill closed dark regions (the header band) with a hachure/cross-hatch fill keyed off the source fill attribute rather than outlining them; keep interior white tick marks as evenodd holes in the filled band.

findings.note: Dark header band renders white/outlined in bold-ink while wet-ink/charcoal/stipple keep it filled. The band's solid value and the white tick-mark knockouts both fail to read.
findings.researchedFix: bold-ink should ink filled source regions as solid/dense fills (its namesake heaviness) and preserve interior knockouts via evenodd compound paths, instead of converting the filled band to an empty outline.

findings.note: Clean boot is a light/white body with diagonal lace hachure marks and a thin outline. risograph fills the ENTIRE boot as a uniform medium-gray solid mass; the diagonal lace marks and the light body are swallowed into a featureless fill. All other variants (incl. stipple/newsprint/charcoal) keep the body light and the lace marks legible.
findings.researchedFix: risograph should be a duotone/halftone screen, not a flat fill: convert tone to a halftone dot screen at a chosen LPI and lift the mid-tones (Tone Lift) so light body areas stay paper-reserve and dark interior marks keep contrast, rather than collapsing shape into one heavy ink mass.

findings.note: Clean map is a LIGHT-gray rectangle with dark, legible interior content: compass 'N', three curved path lines, and an 'X'. risograph fills the rectangle with a uniform DARKER gray that crushes contrast so the curves, N and X nearly merge into the fill. outline-only/wireframe/stipple/charcoal keep the interior content clearly legible.
findings.researchedFix: Render risograph fill as a screened halftone (dots/lines) at the source tone value with mid-tone lift so a region that is LIGHT in Clean stays light enough for the dark line work to read; reserve solid ink only for genuinely dark source regions.

findings.note: Clean source is a dark (dk 0.95) filled rectangle. rod-q35/q315 render a WHITE box with only a thin outline and faint detail line; auto/extrude/solid render it dark. The rod mesh ignores the source's dark surface value and renders bare/white.
findings.researchedFix: Apply the source SVG as a texture/material on the generated rod mesh: build explicit UVs on the procedural geometry and map the source artwork (or its tone) onto the front face so the dark fill carries through, instead of leaving the mesh on a default white material.

findings.note: inflate-q35/q315 produce a puffy outlined form whose interior is WHITE/empty; the dark source surface is dropped (only the silhouette outline and a faint mark survive). auto/extrude/solid keep it dark.
findings.researchedFix: After Monster-Mash-style single-view inflation, texture the inflated mesh with the source artwork via UVs (front-facing projection) so the dark fill and interior marks ride the surface; the inflation should carry the source image as a texture, not just produce a bare balloon mesh.

findings.note: Dark (dk 0.97) source; rod-q35/q315 render a white box with faint inner rectangle + small circle outline, surface white. auto/extrude/solid render dark. Same rod white-surface failure.
findings.researchedFix: Texture the rod mesh's front face with the source artwork via explicit UVs so the dark surface value renders, rather than defaulting to white.

findings.note: inflate-q35/q315 give a puffy white-interior form; dark source surface dropped, only faint rectangle remains.
findings.researchedFix: Project the source image as a texture onto the inflated mesh (UV-mapped front projection) so surface tone is preserved post-inflation.

findings.note: Clean flyer has clear interior content: a header box, a zigzag scribble, and several text lines (visible in rod/inflate which keep them). extrude-q35/q315 render a solid dark slab where this interior content is swallowed into the fill (only faint scratches survive). auto and solid lose it the same way.
findings.researchedFix: Drive the extruded front face with a displacement/relief map derived from the source artwork (bas-relief from the drawing): use per-pixel extrusion / displacement so interior lines become surface micro-relief that catches light, or texture-map the source onto the front face, instead of a flat dark extrusion that flattens detail.

findings.note: solid-q35/q315 also bury the header box, zigzag and text lines in a uniform dark mass; the content that rod/inflate preserve is lost.
findings.researchedFix: Apply a depth-compressed bas-relief displacement from the source (Laplacian-coordinate detail preservation / arctangent gradient compression) to the solid front face so fine interior features survive as relief instead of collapsing into the fill.

findings.note: Dark (dk 0.98) source; rod-q35/q315 render a white-surfaced outlined form with faint top detail line. Surface tone dropped vs dark auto/extrude/solid.
findings.researchedFix: UV-map the source artwork onto the rod mesh front face so its dark surface renders rather than a default white material.

findings.note: inflate-q35/q315 produce a white-interior puffy form with the handwritten setlist detail dropped.
findings.researchedFix: Texture the inflated mesh with the source image (front projection UVs) so surface tone and handwritten marks are preserved after inflation.

findings.note: Clean has a prominent circle (disc/logo) plus panel lines, clearly visible in rod/inflate. extrude-q35/q315 (and auto) render a dark slab where the circle is swallowed to a barely-visible faint ring. Cover content lost in the extrusion.
findings.researchedFix: Use the source artwork as a displacement/bas-relief map on the extruded front face so the circle and panel lines become surface relief that catches light; per-pixel extrusion mapping stores the shape pattern in a texture and keeps it visible on the extruded box.

findings.note: rod-q35/q315 render the magazine as a white box (surface tone dropped). The circle/panel detail is preserved as outline, but the dark source surface value is lost vs the dark auto/extrude/solid renders.
findings.researchedFix: UV-texture the rod front face with the source artwork so the dark cover surface renders while keeping the circle/panel detail.

findings.note: Clean cover has rich layout: a circle (disc), a square panel, and lines, all legible in rod/inflate. extrude-q35/q315 and auto render a dark slab that swallows the circle, square and lines into the fill. solid partially embosses the circle but most layout is lost.
findings.researchedFix: Bas-relief / displacement-map the front face from the source artwork (depth-compressed with detail preservation) so the disc, panel and lines survive as surface relief; alternatively UV-map the source as an albedo/relief texture onto the extruded front face.

findings.note: inflate-q35/q315 render a puffy white-interior form; the dark cover surface is dropped (circle/square preserved as distorted outline only).
findings.researchedFix: Texture the inflated mesh with the source image via front-projection UVs so surface tone is preserved post-inflation; constrain inflation distortion (ARAP-L rigidity) so the layout marks stay recognizable.

findings.note: CLEAN is a solid-black square (closed map). inflate renders a puffy form as an OUTLINE only with a WHITE interior, with fold-grid lines floating in the empty white. The solid dark body of Clean is gone; the inflated surface is treated as a transparent/wireframe shell rather than a filled opaque solid. rod is correctly an outline (wireframe mode), but inflate is supposed to be a filled shaded solid like auto/extrude/solid, all of which stay dark.
findings.researchedFix: Inflate should close and fill the silhouette into a watertight rotund solid (Teddy/Igarashi sketch inflation: triangulate the interior of the closed silhouette, inflate the region so wide areas are fat and narrow thin, then shade the front faces opaque) — not leave the front face transparent showing the back. The closed sketch must drive a BASE/solid sweep, not a thin-feature shell.

findings.note: CLEAN is a solid-black rectangle (dk 0.94). inflate is an outlined puffy panel with a WHITE interior, horizontal bars showing through the empty fill. Same hollow-shell problem: the opaque dark fill of Clean becomes transparent. auto/extrude/solid all correctly stay dark.

findings.note: CLEAN shows a round plush with ears and a visible FACE (two eye dots + smile). extrude (q35/q315) renders a solid dark sphere with ears but the face — eyes and smile — is completely swallowed into the featureless dark form. rod and inflate both retain the eyes/smile; only the flat-shaded extrude (and auto) drop them.
findings.researchedFix: Carry the interior face strokes onto the extruded/inflated surface as a bas-relief displacement (signed displacement map along surface normals from the 2D detail layer), so eyes/smile emboss into the dark form instead of being flattened away. Decompose into smooth base + detail layer and re-apply the detail layer post-extrusion.

findings.note: auto (q35/q315) produces the same featureless dark sphere with ears as extrude — the face (eyes + smile) present in CLEAN is lost into the solid form.
findings.researchedFix: Same bas-relief detail-layer re-application: separate base geometry from the face detail layer and emboss the detail as normal-direction displacement so interior marks survive solid shading.

findings.note: CLEAN shows a small figurine with tiny eye dots on the head. extrude renders a solid dark figure with the face/eyes lost into the dark form. rod and inflate keep the eye dots visible; the flat-shaded dark modes drop them.
findings.researchedFix: Re-apply the facial detail layer as displacement/bas-relief on the extruded body (base+detail decomposition, signed displacement along normals) so the eyes emboss rather than vanish.

findings.note: CLEAN is a belt buckle whose ring/loop has an OPEN center. extrude (and auto/solid) fills the buckle into a featureless solid dark mass — the open ring hole is gone. rod and inflate correctly preserve the open loop/holes.
findings.researchedFix: Treat the buckle outline as a polygon WITH HOLES: triangulate using bridge edges (or even-odd fill rule) so the inner loop stays open, then extrude both the outer and inner boundaries to a genus-1 solid. Do not flood-fill the whole silhouette.

findings.note: CLEAN is a solid-black card (dk 0.94). inflate renders the card as a puffy OUTLINE with a WHITE interior panel and a portrait figure floating in the empty fill. Clean's opaque dark body is replaced by transparency. auto/extrude/solid stay correctly dark.
findings.researchedFix: Fill the inflated card silhouette as an opaque solid (Teddy inflation closes and fills the region), and treat the portrait/panel as surface displacement on the dark front face rather than a white knockout.

findings.note: CLEAN is a solid-black square (dk 0.95). inflate is an outlined puffy form with a WHITE interior and fold-grid lines in the empty fill — opaque dark body dropped to a transparent shell. auto/extrude/solid stay dark.
findings.researchedFix: Close+fill the inflated silhouette to an opaque watertight solid (Teddy skin algorithm), with fold lines as surface displacement, not transparency.

findings.note: CLEAN is a solid-black can shape. inflate renders a puffy can OUTLINE with a WHITE interior and bubble dots floating in the empty fill. Opaque dark body of Clean lost to a hollow shell. auto/extrude/solid stay dark.
findings.researchedFix: Inflate the closed silhouette into an opaque filled solid (Teddy), shading front faces dark to occlude the back; bubbles become surface detail/displacement, not white knockouts.

findings.note: CLEAN is a solid-black rectangle (poster, dk 0.92). inflate renders a puffy poster OUTLINE with WHITE interior and a bottle illustration in the empty fill. Opaque dark body replaced by transparency. auto/extrude/solid stay dark.
findings.researchedFix: Triangulate+fill the inflated silhouette as an opaque solid (Teddy inflation), with the bottle as displacement detail on the dark front face.

findings.note: CLEAN is a small solid-black bar. inflate renders a puffy wedge OUTLINE with a WHITE interior and slanted lines in the empty fill. Opaque dark body of Clean dropped. auto/extrude/solid stay dark.
findings.researchedFix: Close and fill the inflated silhouette interior as an opaque solid (Teddy), shading the front surface dark; interior lines as displacement.

findings.note: CLEAN shows a headband ARC plus two separated earcups with concentric-ring detail. extrude (q35/q315) collapses everything into a single featureless dark lumpy MASS — the open headband arc and the gap between band and earcups are gone, earcup rings lost. rod, inflate, and solid all preserve the arc + ringed earcups; extrude is the failure.
findings.researchedFix: Preserve thin/branching features and concavities before extruding: detect them via medial-axis significance so the open arc and the band-to-cup gap are not flooded, and treat the silhouette as a multi-region polygon with holes (concentric earcup rings = holes). Extrude per-region with the open arc kept hollow rather than filling the convex hull.

findings.note: CLEAN is a tiny solid-dark teardrop pick (dk 0.89). inflate renders an empty RING/outline with a WHITE interior — the solid pick body is gone, leaving only a rim. auto/extrude/solid all stay correctly dark and filled.
findings.researchedFix: Inflate must fill the closed teardrop silhouette into an opaque rounded solid (Teddy: wide region = fat, opaque front shading), not produce a hollow tube/rim.

findings.note: CLEAN is a solid-black rectangle (dk 0.94). inflate renders a puffy cartridge OUTLINE with a WHITE interior and label lines in the empty fill. Opaque dark body dropped to transparent shell. auto/extrude/solid stay dark.
findings.researchedFix: Close+fill the inflated silhouette as an opaque solid (Teddy), label as surface displacement on the dark face.

findings.note: CLEAN is a fully-black thin vertical bar (dk 1.00 — maximum darkness). inflate renders a hollow loop/OUTLINE with a WHITE interior. Most extreme case: a 100%-black object becomes an empty ring. auto/extrude/solid stay solid dark.
findings.researchedFix: Fill the inflated closed silhouette into an opaque solid (Teddy inflation); a dk 1.00 source must map to a fully opaque dark surface, never a transparent shell.

findings.note: CLEAN is a solid-black bar (dk 0.94). inflate renders a puffy clapperboard OUTLINE with a WHITE slate interior and clapper stripes in the empty fill. Opaque dark body dropped. auto/extrude/solid stay dark.
findings.researchedFix: Triangulate+fill the inflated silhouette as an opaque solid (Teddy); slate lines/stripes as displacement on the dark front face.

findings.note: CLEAN is a fully-black rectangle (dk 1.00). inflate renders a puffy pack OUTLINE with a WHITE interior and bands in the empty fill — another dk 1.00 source rendering as a transparent shell. auto/extrude/solid stay solid dark.
findings.researchedFix: Close+fill the inflated silhouette to an opaque solid (Teddy); dk 1.00 must shade fully opaque dark, bands as displacement.

findings.note: CLEAN is a solid-black horizontal handheld bar. inflate renders a puffy OUTLINE with a WHITE screen and buttons floating in the empty fill. Opaque dark body dropped. auto/extrude/solid stay dark.
findings.researchedFix: Fill the inflated silhouette interior opaque (Teddy); screen/buttons as surface displacement, not white knockout.

findings.note: CLEAN is a solid-black square. inflate renders a puffy OUTLINE with a WHITE interior and center hub in the empty fill. Opaque dark body dropped to a transparent shell. auto/extrude/solid stay dark.

findings.note: CLEAN is a small solid-dark megaphone (dk 0.94). inflate renders a puffy megaphone OUTLINE with a WHITE interior and lines in the empty fill. Opaque dark body dropped. auto/extrude/solid stay dark.
