findings.note: CLEAN is a solid-black rectangle (dk 0.97). inflate renders a puffy suitcase OUTLINE with a WHITE interior, handle and wheels in the empty fill. Opaque dark body dropped to a transparent shell. auto/extrude/solid stay dark.
findings.researchedFix: Close+fill the inflated silhouette as an opaque solid (Teddy); handle/wheels/seams as surface displacement on the dark front face.

findings.note: CLEAN is a ring = round BAND with an open center hole + a triangular gem on top. extrude (and auto/solid) fills the band's open center into a solid dark DISC — the defining hole is gone, turning the ring into a lollipop/disc. rod and inflate correctly preserve the open hole (true torus). Inverse failure: a region that should be open/white is shaded solid.
findings.researchedFix: Treat the ring outline as a polygon WITH A HOLE: triangulate with bridge edges (or even-odd fill rule) so the band's center stays open, then extrude both boundaries into a genus-1 torus solid. Do not fill the silhouette convex region.

findings.note: auto (q35/q315) makes the same mistake as extrude: the ring's open center is filled into a solid dark disc, losing the hole that defines a ring. inflate/rod keep the hole.
findings.researchedFix: Same hole-preserving triangulation (polygon-with-holes via bridge edges or even-odd rule) before generating geometry, so the auto path produces a torus rather than a filled disc.

findings.note: Clean (and rod/inflate) show the lens ring + viewfinder rectangle + small dot on the camera face. extrude-q35/q315 render a featureless dark body (blackFrac 0.798/0.558 vs rod 0.013), and auto-q35/q315 are identical to extrude (same stats) — the lens/viewfinder face marks vanish into the slab. solid retains them only faintly.
findings.researchedFix: Deboss/engrave the interior face strokes onto the extruded front face via a displacement (height-map) pass on a subdivided face cap, instead of leaving ExtrudeGeometry's flat filled cap. ExtrudeGeometry alone fills the outer contour and discards interior lines; a lithophane-style Displace pass (image/line-art -> grayscale heightmap -> offset subdivided cap) re-imprints the lens/viewfinder as relief — which is exactly why the inflate/rod modes keep them.

findings.note: rod/inflate show a disc with 3 horizontal grille bars + center hub. extrude-q35/q315 (and auto, identical stats) render a plain dark disc (blackFrac 0.801/0.549 vs rod 0.024) — the grille bars and hub disappear into the solid disc.
findings.researchedFix: Engrave the grille bars + hub as a displacement/normal-map relief on the disc's flat face rather than capping the extrusion solid; differential-coordinate / high-relief detail preservation keeps interior feature lines as depth discontinuities on the extruded cap.

findings.note: Clean/rod/auto show a cone strainer + a thin hanging STRING and a small bottom knot. extrude-q35/q315 render the cone as a solid dark mass (blackFrac 0.895/0.698, bboxFill 0.59 vs auto 0.17) and the thin hanging string element is dropped entirely — only the cone survives, fattened.
findings.researchedFix: Classify the thin string as an OPEN stroke and sweep it into a thin tube (open path -> surface/tube) instead of letting the extruder fold it into the cone's filled region. Open vs closed contour detection: closed regions inflate/extrude to solids, open curves become swept tubes/connectors.

findings.note: Clean blackish=0.00 — it is a thin OPEN squiggle stroke with an empty (white) interior; auto and rod faithfully keep it as a thin line (blackFrac 0.007). extrude-q35/q315 flood-fill the squiggle into a solid black ribbon/blob (blackFrac 0.807/0.506) — an open stroke wrongly treated as a closed fillable region. solid is also overweight (0.582) though still legible.
findings.researchedFix: Detect the path is OPEN (no closepath / endpoints not coincident) and sweep it into a constant-radius tube along the polyline rather than filling it as a polygon. Sweeping an open profile yields a surface/tube; only closed contours should be filled to solids.

findings.note: rod shows an emblem (triangle/heart) and a hole inside the opener's round head. extrude-q35/q315 (and auto, identical stats, blackFrac 0.859/0.501 vs rod 0.005) render the head as a featureless dark paddle — the head emblem/hole drops out. inflate/solid retain the emblem.
findings.researchedFix: Engrave the head emblem/hole as a displacement relief (or boolean cut for the through-hole) on the extruded head cap; height-map deboss on a subdivided face preserves the interior emblem instead of a flat filled cap.

findings.note: rod shows a regular GRID (contact-sheet cells). extrude-q35/q315 (and auto, blackFrac 0.797/0.562 vs rod 0.008) render a flat dark slab; the grid lines vanish. inflate keeps the grid embossed.
findings.researchedFix: Deboss the grid as a relief/displacement pass on the panel's extruded face (line-art -> grayscale heightmap -> Displace on a subdivided cap), the lithophane-style engraving the inflate mode already applies.

findings.note: rod shows the lid covered in distinct STICKERS (rounded rects, circles). extrude-q35/q315 (and auto, blackFrac 0.798/0.555 vs rod 0.013) render a blank dark slab — every sticker disappears, erasing the object's defining feature. inflate/solid keep stickers as embossed shapes.
findings.researchedFix: Engrave the sticker shapes onto the extruded face via displacement/normal-map relief instead of a flat filled cap; high-relief detail-preservation keeps the interior sticker contours as depth discontinuities.

findings.note: rod shows the framed shot's interior UI panels/cards. extrude-q35/q315 (and auto, blackFrac 0.792/0.564 vs rod 0.011) collapse it to a dark slab; the framed artwork is gone. inflate/solid retain embossed panels.
findings.researchedFix: Deboss the framed interior art as a displacement-map relief on the front face (line-art heightmap -> Displace on subdivided cap), preserving panel lines as relief rather than a flat fill.

findings.note: rod shows a framed poster with a central emblem (arched dome/sun motif). extrude-q35/q315 (and auto, blackFrac 0.786/0.578 vs rod 0.043) render a dark slab; the poster emblem vanishes. inflate/solid keep it embossed.
findings.researchedFix: Engrave the poster emblem as relief via image-to-heightmap displacement on the extruded face cap rather than filling the cap solid.

findings.note: rod shows a character FACE (two eyes + smile) on the round head atop an oval base. extrude-q35/q315 (and auto, blackFrac 0.730/0.491 vs rod 0.035) render the head as a featureless dark ball — the face is lost. inflate/solid retain eyes/smile.
findings.researchedFix: Treat the face as interior feature lines and deboss them onto the head surface via displacement/normal relief (bas-relief from line art), the technique the inflate mode already uses; do not cap the extrusion as a flat fill.

findings.note: rod shows a plush face (eyes + smile + cheeks) with ears. extrude-q35/q315 (and auto, blackFrac 0.756/0.481 vs rod 0.045) become a solid dark head-blob — the face merges away. inflate/solid keep the face as relief.
findings.researchedFix: Bas-relief / displacement engraving of the face onto the inflated head surface (grayscale line-art heightmap -> Displace), preserving eyes/smile as depth instead of a featureless cap.

findings.note: rod shows text LINES + a HEART at the bottom of the letter. extrude-q35/q315 (and auto, blackFrac 0.786/0.577 vs rod 0.025) render a flat dark slab; text and heart vanish. solid/inflate retain them embossed.
findings.researchedFix: Deboss the text lines + heart onto the extruded page face via lithophane-style displacement (line-art -> heightmap -> Displace on subdivided cap) instead of a flat filled cap.

findings.note: rod shows an inset (WHITE knockout) label panel on the cover. extrude-q35/q315 (and auto, blackFrac 0.787/0.577 vs rod 0.039) fill the whole cover dark — the inset label panel that is white/recessed in Clean is shaded over. solid/inflate keep the panel.
findings.researchedFix: Respect the knockout/inset region: cut/recess it as an inner relief step (negative displacement or boolean inset) so the white panel reads as a recessed face, rather than flooding the entire cover cap solid. ExtrudeGeometry hole/inner-contour handling preserves inner regions.

findings.note: rod shows a controller silhouette (figure-8 body + two button circles) inside the shadow box. extrude-q35/q315 (and auto, blackFrac 0.792/0.566 vs rod 0.018) render a blank dark slab; the controller is gone. solid/inflate retain it embossed.
findings.researchedFix: Engrave the controller silhouette as relief on the box's front face via displacement (line-art heightmap -> Displace on subdivided cap), keeping interior feature lines as depth.

findings.note: rod shows the TV's SCREEN filled with horizontal scanlines (its defining feature). extrude-q35/q315 (and auto, blackFrac 0.814/0.555 vs rod 0.006) render a dark slab; screen + scanlines vanish. solid/inflate retain the scanline screen.
findings.researchedFix: Recess the screen as an inset face and deboss the scanlines via displacement relief on it (inset inner contour + line-art heightmap Displace) instead of a flat solid cap.

findings.note: rod/inflate variants in the same row clearly carry the interior line-art (spiral binding rings down the left edge + a wave doodle on the cover). extrude-q35 collapses the whole face into a featureless dark slab (measured blackFrac 0.784) - binding rings and doodle are gone. This is the single clearest instance of the dominant systematic failure. auto-q35 is byte-identical to extrude-q35 (auto just routes to extrude), and solid-q35 shows the same blob; only inflate and the lighter q315 angle keep the marks.
findings.researchedFix: Do not let extrusion present a flat unlit cap. Project the source line-art onto the extruded front face as real surface relief: emboss/deboss/scribe the strokes (SolidWorks 'Wrap' style), or apply a bas-relief displacement map / subdivision-surface engraving driven by the 2D drawing's pixel values, so interior strokes survive as ridges/grooves instead of being flattened. For pure visual fidelity a decal/texture projection of the clean strokes onto the cap is the lightweight equivalent.

findings.note: Same family. rod/inflate show a framed photo: a white frame border (knockout) around a figure silhouette. extrude-q35 (blackFrac 0.784, also auto-q35 and solid-q35) renders one solid black box - both the white frame border and the interior figure are absorbed into the mass. The white frame knockout being filled is also a white-shaded component.
findings.researchedFix: Triangulate the extrusion profile with the even-odd fill rule so the inner frame contour stays a hole through the depth (keeps the white knockout), AND emboss/displacement-map the interior figure onto the cap face per the bas-relief technique above so the silhouette is not flattened.

findings.note: rod/inflate show the speaker grille (horizontal slats) and the top row of control knobs. extrude-q35 / auto-q35 / solid-q35 (blackFrac 0.795) flatten to a dark slab; grille slats and knobs vanish.
findings.researchedFix: Emboss/deboss the grille slats and knob circles onto the extruded face as displacement relief (bas-relief / Wrap), rather than producing a blank cap.

findings.note: Worst blob of the set (blackFrac 0.895). rod shows slatted seat/back + leg frame; extrude-q35 / auto-q35 are a near-pure black mass, all slats and the leg structure lost. solid-q35 (0.710) partially recovers; inflate keeps the slats.
findings.researchedFix: Same bas-relief/emboss treatment for the slat lines; additionally because the chair has open gaps between slats and legs, triangulate the profile with even-odd fill so those gaps stay as holes instead of being filled solid.

findings.note: rod shows the screen rectangle + d-pad + face buttons. extrude-q35 / auto-q35 / solid-q35 (blackFrac 0.831) flatten to a dark slab; screen and controls gone. q315 angle and inflate keep them.
findings.researchedFix: Deboss the screen recess and emboss the control marks onto the extruded cap via displacement/Wrap relief; the recessed screen specifically wants an extruded-cut, not a flat fill.

findings.note: rod shows D-pad (+), analog/button cluster, action buttons. extrude-q35 / auto-q35 (blackFrac 0.827) flatten to a dark gamepad blob; buttons lost. inflate and solid-q35 keep them.
findings.researchedFix: Emboss the button/d-pad marks onto the cap as relief (bas-relief displacement / Wrap); convex buttons should be positive displacement, recessed d-pad negative.

findings.note: rod/inflate show popcorn kernels heaped at the top and the vertical box stripes. extrude-q35 / auto-q35 / solid-q35 (blackFrac 0.743) flatten to a dark bucket mass; kernels and stripes lost.
findings.researchedFix: Emboss the stripe lines and inflate the kernel cluster as positive relief on the extruded form (per-part inflation / displacement), instead of a flat cap.

findings.note: Clean is a head+body+ears silhouette; rod/inflate render two eyes on the face. extrude-q35 / auto-q35 / solid-q35 (blackFrac 0.746) absorb the face into the dark form - the eyes (the only interior marks) vanish. This is the 'face's eyes vanish into the form' case named in the brief.
findings.researchedFix: Inflate the silhouette to a rounded (semi-elliptical) profile and deboss the eyes as concave marks via displacement/bas-relief, the way drawing-to-relief reconstruction inflates each semantic part and stamps interior features.

findings.note: rod shows the printed card-zone layout (two rectangles + a circle). extrude-q35 / auto-q35 / solid-q35 (blackFrac 0.809) flatten to a black rectangle; zone graphics lost.
findings.researchedFix: The zone lines are a flat print, not geometry - project them as a decal/texture onto the extruded top face (decal route is the correct one for purely visual surface graphics), or lightly scribe them with Wrap.

findings.note: rod shows a top band + a mountain-range illustration. extrude-q35 / auto-q35 (blackFrac 0.794) flatten to a black tile; illustration and band lost. inflate keeps them.
findings.researchedFix: Decal/texture-project the mountain illustration onto the extruded face (flat printed art = decal), and emboss the band seam.

findings.note: rod/inflate show the vertical pack ridges (white striping). extrude-q35 / auto-q35 / solid-q35 (blackFrac 0.792) flatten to a black box; ridges lost.
findings.researchedFix: Emboss the vertical ridges as repeating relief grooves on the extruded face (Wrap / displacement).

findings.note: rod/inflate show the passport cover emblem + seal marks. extrude-q35 / auto-q35 / solid-q35 (blackFrac 0.792) flatten to a black book; emblem lost.
findings.researchedFix: Emboss the cover emblem/seal onto the extruded cap as gold-foil-style relief (positive displacement / Wrap).

findings.note: rod/inflate show the figure-in-package: blister card with the wrestler silhouette. extrude-q35 / auto-q35 (blackFrac 0.787) flatten to a black slab; figure and card frame lost.
findings.researchedFix: Inflate the blister bubble as a raised dome and deboss the card frame; emboss the figure silhouette via bas-relief displacement.

findings.note: rod/inflate/solid show the stick + button details; extrude-q35 / auto-q35 (blackFrac 0.797) flatten to a dark bar, controls lost.
findings.researchedFix: Emboss the analog-stick recess and buttons onto the extruded face via displacement/Wrap.

findings.note: rod shows the cover emblem circle; extrude-q35 / auto-q35 / solid-q35 (blackFrac 0.785) flatten to a black book, emblem lost.
findings.researchedFix: Emboss the emblem onto the extruded cover as relief (Wrap / displacement).

findings.note: rod shows the lens circle + viewfinder; extrude-q35 / auto-q35 / solid-q35 (blackFrac 0.774) flatten to a black body, lens lost. inflate keeps the lens.
findings.researchedFix: Extrude-cut the lens recess (it is a recessed cylinder, not a flat mark) and emboss the viewfinder, per extruded-cut + Wrap.

findings.note: Clean is a coiled cable (concentric loops + connector). rod/inflate render the spiral coil; extrude-q35 / auto-q35 / solid-q35 (blackFrac 0.773) collapse it to a featureless solid disc - the coil pattern is gone.
findings.researchedFix: A coil is a swept tube, not a fillable disc: model it as a sweep along the spiral path (swept profile), or at minimum triangulate with even-odd fill so the gaps between coil rings remain holes instead of one solid disc.

findings.note: rod/inflate show the cap seam line dividing cap from barrel; extrude-q35 / auto-q35 (blackFrac 0.796) render a uniform dark pen, seam lost. Minor (single interior line) but real.
findings.researchedFix: Scribe the cap seam as a debossed groove (Wrap) across the extruded barrel.

findings.note: Representative of the whole rod-q35 column (every object): the rod mode renders only a thin hollow outline / wireframe shell (objFrac ~0.02-0.09, blackFrac ~0.01-0.06) where Clean is a solidly inked object. The filled silhouette is dropped to an empty frame - the form reads as not-there at the steep angle. q315 rod is slightly darker but still mostly hollow.
findings.researchedFix: Cap the extrusion (add front/back end faces) and ensure correct face winding + back-face culling so the solid silhouette is rendered rather than a see-through wireframe; a filled extruded solid should never present as outline-only.

findings.note: Clean shows a key fob with an open ring/loop (white hole). extrude-q35 / auto-q35 / solid-q35 fill the loop into a solid dark disc (blackFrac 0.69-0.74) - the white knockout of the ring is shaded over. inflate/rod keep the loop open.
findings.researchedFix: Triangulate the extrusion profile with the even-odd fill rule so the ring's inner contour is preserved as a through-hole instead of being filled; this is the standard polygon-with-holes capping that keeps interior knockouts.

findings.note: Clean is a solid dark filled pill/cylinder (dk 0.93). Rod renders an outline-only white cylinder with a few longitudinal lines; the dark body fill is dropped entirely, so the form reads empty/light instead of dark.
findings.researchedFix: Rod/skeleton modes must carry the source SVG's solid fill onto the generated 3D surface rather than re-deriving as feature-line outlines. The Monster Mash pipeline inflates the 2D region and 'uses the template image as a texture of the final 3D model', so filled regions stay filled; apply the Clean SVG (with its dark fill) as a front-face/projected texture on the rod's swept surface instead of stroking only the silhouette.

findings.note: Clean dark fill becomes a puffy outline form with a white/empty interior; only the rim and a few hachure lines are inked. The body that is solid dark in Clean reads light.
findings.researchedFix: Inflate the closed region (boundary-to-medial half-circle profile per Monster Mash / mesh-inflation stroke method) AND texture the inflated front face with the original drawing so the dark fill is preserved; do not render the inflated mesh as an unfilled contour. Monster Mash explicitly supports tracing over a template image and reusing it as the model texture.

findings.note: Clean is a solid dark disc + handle (dk 0.90). Rod renders the disc as an empty white ring/outline; the filled pan face is dropped to outline-only.
findings.researchedFix: Region fill must survive the skeleton/rod conversion: extract the filled region, then project the source fill as a texture onto the swept rod surface (Monster Mash template-as-texture). The disc region should remain a filled cap, not a wireframe ring.

findings.note: Inflated disc becomes a puffy white ring with concentric outline; dark fill of the pan face dropped to empty interior.
findings.researchedFix: Use stroke-extraction + mesh inflation that joins boundary point pairs with half-circles to build the cap, then bake the Clean drawing onto the inflated front face so the dark region stays dark.

findings.note: Clean is a solid dark bag silhouette with handle + flap + clasp (dk 0.93). Rod renders the whole bag as a white outline drawing; the dark body fill is gone.
findings.researchedFix: Carry the filled silhouette through the rod conversion as a textured surface rather than feature-line outline; project the source SVG fill onto the generated geometry (Monster Mash template-texture approach).

findings.note: Inflated bag is a puffy outline with white interior; only the clasp and edges are inked. Dark body fill dropped.
findings.researchedFix: Inflate the closed bag region and texture the inflated front face with the Clean drawing so the dark fill is retained; clasp/flap should be a displacement/relief detail on a filled surface, not the only inked element.

findings.note: Clean is two solid dark beads joined by a cord (dk 0.86). Rod renders the beads as empty white rings/outlines; bead fill dropped.
findings.researchedFix: Preserve per-region fill when sweeping rods through the bead centers: project the source fill onto each bead's swept surface (template-as-texture) so beads read solid dark, not as rings.

findings.note: Inflated beads become puffy concentric-spiral outlines with white interior; dark bead fill dropped.

findings.researchedFix: Keep the frame inset as a real geometric step (inner profile extruded to a shallower depth) and project the portrait linework onto the recessed face via decal/displacement. SVGLoader supports nested shapes/holes so the frame opening can be modeled as a true inset rather than flattened.

Monster Mash's region-aware inflation specifically preserves interior stroke relationships when going 2D->3D.

findings.researchedFix: Apply the fold/collar lines as a normal+displacement map on the inflated cloth body so soft seams read as relief; inflation (rounded cross-section) plus displacement is the established cloth-from-sketch approach rather than flat prism extrusion.

findings.researchedFix: Bake the key-grid SVG as a displacement/height map so each keycap is a small raised relief on the extruded body; displacement is specifically recommended where engraved/relief macro detail (like keycaps) must survive on the silhouette.

findings.researchedFix: Use even-odd/nonzero fill-rule-aware geometry so the center hole is preserved, and bake the concentric grooves as a circular displacement/height map on the disc face. For radial groove detail a height-map-to-relief pass is the standard approach.

findings.note: Clean/rod/inflate/solid show the bottle with a label window and cap detail. extrude-q35/q315 and auto-q35/q315 render a plain dark bottle silhouette; the label/sticker detail is lost.

findings.note: CLEAN medal disc is a SOLID dark circle. Both inflate angles turn the disc into a hollow donut/torus with a white empty center, and the ribbon clip into an open loop. The inflater is puffing the boundary OUTLINE into a tube instead of filling the enclosed disc region, so a solid disc reads as a ring with a knockout hole. auto/extrude/solid all render the solid disc faithfully; only inflate fails.
findings.researchedFix: Inflate the FILLED region bounded by the closed silhouette (not the stroke): build an interior distance/height field and raise it into a rounded solid cross-section (Teddy chordal-axis fattening — wide areas fat, narrow areas thin), so a solid disc becomes a puffed lens with no center hole.

findings.note: CLEAN is a compact SOLID faceted moka-pot silhouette (octagonal body + handle + lid knob). Both inflate angles decompose it into balloon tube-loops: the body becomes two stacked rounded blobs (figure-8) and the handle a large hollow loop, with white interiors. The characteristic moka-pot silhouette is destroyed because each sub-contour is inflated as an independent tube rather than the whole region as one connected solid. auto/extrude/solid keep the silhouette.
findings.researchedFix: Treat the closed silhouette as a single region and inflate to a connected SOLID mesh with rounded cross-section by solving a modified Poisson equation over the interior (Monster Mash single-view inflation), so the filled body puffs as one solid form instead of separate hollow tubes.

findings.note: CLEAN is a SOLID dark ellipse (smooth pebble, no hole). Both inflate angles render a swirled hollow torus with concentric rings and a white/empty center; the surface thumb-dimple becomes a through-hole. The solid pebble should puff to a filled lens. Boundary-tube inflation again hollows the interior. auto/extrude/solid render it as a solid lens with the dimple as surface relief.
findings.researchedFix: Inflate the interior region via a distance-transform height field into a solid puffed lens (Teddy / inflation_py silhouette-to-heightfield), keeping the thumb dimple as a shallow surface displacement rather than a through-hole.

findings.note: CLEAN is a SOLID dark canister (cylindrical body, cap, tapered base). Both inflate angles render a hollow inflated tube/frame: only the outline is puffed into a rounded border while the interior goes white/empty, so the solid body reads as an empty ring outline. auto/extrude/solid render the canister as a filled solid.
findings.researchedFix: Fill-region inflation: raise the enclosed silhouette area into a rounded solid cross-section (Teddy inflation of the region surrounded by the silhouette), producing a puffed solid pillow with no hollow interior, instead of inflating only the boundary stroke.
